note: Plan-only prompts on fresh `claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --tools "" --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --output-format json` sessions in an empty folder; the prompt goes in on stdin. Control without the skill; the with-skill run gets this SKILL.md and triaging-issues' SKILL.md (the skill its step 1 points to) prepended. Grade from the answer text. Each run records the model and session id from the CLI's JSON result (`modelUsage`, `session_id`), elapsed time, cost and tokens; input tokens include about 254k of harness and user context that every run shares. The control's answer is kept verbatim in `control.output`; the raw JSON results go to `results/` (gitignored). Runs 2026-10-14, control and with-skill launched in the same turn. near-miss-triage is a trigger test: the model sees both skill descriptions and names the one it loads (TRIAGE_DESC and PLAN_DESC in the prompt are replaced by the frontmatter descriptions); control uses the description without the closing negative trigger, the with-skill run the current one.

control.output:
## Recommendation

| Milestone | Issues | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **v0.7.1** | #31, #32, #35, #37 | Three crashes and one data-loss bug. This matches the milestone description exactly. |
| **v0.8** | #33, #34, #36, #38, #39 | Features and polish. #36 follows #34, and #38 follows #37, so every dependency lands in the same or an earlier milestone. |

Two calls need your confirmation:

- **#37 (macOS keychain crash) is in scope but at risk.** The agent can't reproduce or test it on Linux. A blind fix to secrets handling shouldn't ship in a patch release. I'd keep it in v0.7.1 only if someone with a Mac verifies it. If nobody has verified it within about a week, move it to v0.8 so it doesn't hold up the release. **Who can test it on macOS?**
- **#33 (typo in `--help`) goes to v0.8** even though it's small. It's polish, not a crash or data loss, and "crash and data-loss fixes only" rules it out. If you'd rather slip it into the patch, say so.

The workload is fine: v0.7.1 has three S issues and one M issue (#32) for two weeks.

## What I'd read first

1. The exact milestone titles, because `gh issue edit --milestone` matches on title, and a check that both are open:
   ```bash
   gh api repos/lorenzh/demo/milestones --jq '.[] | [.number, .title, .state, .due_on] | @tsv'
   ```
2. #37 and #32, to see whether a comment already names a macOS tester or shows #32 is bigger than M:
   ```bash
   gh issue view 37 --repo lorenzh/demo --comments
   gh issue view 32 --repo lorenzh/demo --comments
   ```

I wouldn't re-triage the other issues. The verdicts are fresh.

## Commands I'd run (after your OK on #37 and #33)

```bash
gh issue edit 31 32 35 37 --repo lorenzh/demo --milestone "v0.7.1"
gh issue edit 33 34 36 38 39 --repo lorenzh/demo --milestone "v0.8"

gh issue comment 37 --repo lorenzh/demo --body "In v0.7.1, but it needs verification on macOS before release (no macOS environment available to the agent). If nobody has verified it by about a week before the due date, it moves to v0.8."

# Check the result
gh issue list --repo lorenzh/demo --milestone "v0.7.1" --state open
gh issue list --repo lorenzh/demo --milestone "v0.8" --state open
```

I'd skip new labels such as `needs-macos`, since the comment covers it. Add a label if you track this kind of blocker across repos.
